second_round_truncated_gemma_leg.why: Dims found first-256 truncation of the stored gemma vectors scores 21/32 on its own; rerun the same fusion with that leg, and control for the truncation with 40 random dimension subsets.
second_round_truncated_gemma_leg.dims_note: Dims' later 1000-subset dense-only control gives random-subset mean gold rank 3.995 (sd 0.822) against first-256's 2.40, so truncation itself deepens the ranking; top-1 and top-5 gains stay noise-level. Fusion-side random-subset means (40 draws): z max 3.589 (sd 0.639, min 2.571), RRF 3.675, z 0.5/0.5 3.591 at 256 dims; first-dims fusion 2.371. Fusion inherits most of its depth from the gemma leg.

third_round_halves_gemma_leg.why: Granularity's halves units (max-pooled to the parent) lift gemma's own top-1 on the 20 rows whose books have unit vectors; run the same fusion over that leg to see whether a finer gemma leg lifts the fusion ceiling.
third_round_halves_gemma_leg.metric_note: mean gold rank counts a miss as n_chunks + 1, so the halves leg's deep novel misses inflate its 8.20; Granularity reports mean rank <=6 and mean hit over found rows instead.

rows_35.why: Granularity extended unit vectors to the other three books, so the halves-leg fusion now covers all 35 answerable rows.
rows_35.note: gemma halves 21/30 matches Granularity's own dense-only number on the same 35 rows; z max over whole 768-d gemma reproduces round 1 exactly (24/31/3.029), so the 35-row extension is on the same footing as the earlier rounds.

cross_experiment_note: Three levers now sit side by side: DocFormat's six document formats (no reliable change, Jaccard 0.45-0.57 between the shown fives), Granularity's finer units (halves +2 top-1 over 35 rows, CI -3..+8, top-5 unchanged; sentences lose 4 top-5), and Dims' truncation (32/35 top-5, and mean gold rank 3.00 -> 2.40, p=0.003 against 1 000 random subsets). The shared fact is that gemma's ranking is a near-tie pool: label formatting, grain and dimension changes all reshuffle which near-tied chunk wins, and only the dimension lever changes depth in place. This experiment's shape follows from that — the fusion's top-1 (24-26) sits inside the random-subset band because it inherits a fragile ordering at the top, while its depth gain is robust because depth is read further down the same ranking. RRF k=60, which discards gemma's score magnitudes and keeps only its order, did worse (24/30 at 768-d, 26/32 at 256-d), so the ceiling is not a normalisation artefact. Attribution: the depth finding is Dims' (truncation) and this experiment's (same effect at a later stage); DocFormat's arm contributes the label result (no reliable change, mean rank declared tail-sensitive there) and the 29/34 heading-family number.
